items.physical_scope: The truncated electric field energy of the idealised point charge in vacuum: the shell energy is $q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0)(1/\delta-1/R)$, finite for $0<\delta<R$ but divergent as the inner cutoff $\delta\downarrow0$ for $q\ne0$. The item records this divergence as a property of the point idealisation and explicitly excludes inferences about particle rest mass, self-force, empirical measurement or inconsistency of the framework; finite-energy statements remain those of the compact-source branches.

items.title: The infinite line charge: logarithmic potential, flux normalization and divergent energy
items.strategy:
For (a): on the open set $\Omega$ ([[def-metric-topology]]; $\rho>0$ is the preimage of the open half-line under the continuous $\rho$, [[thm-continuity-preimage-characterisation]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]) the function $\rho$ is smooth — it is the composition of $x\mapsto x_1^2+x_2^2$ with the square root, positive on $\Omega$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) — and the chain rule together with the logarithm derivative gives $\nabla\varphi=-\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{1}{\rho}\hat e_r=-E$ ([[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).
For (b): with $E_i=\lambda x_i/(2\pi\varepsilon_0\rho^2)$, direct differentiation on $\Omega$ gives $\partial_1E_1+\partial_2E_2=\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{(\rho^2-2x_1^2)+(\rho^2-2x_2^2)}{\rho^4}=0$ and $\partial_1E_2-\partial_2E_1=\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{-2x_1x_2+2x_1x_2}{\rho^4}=0$; the third components vanish since $E_3=0$ and nothing depends on $x_3$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). The electrostatic reading is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (c).
For (c): the displayed map is $C^1$ on an open neighbourhood of the compact Jordan region $D:=[0,2\pi]\times[-L/2,L/2]$; writing $u(\theta)=\operatorname{Re}e^{i\theta}$, $v(\theta)=\operatorname{Im}e^{i\theta}$, the derivative $\frac{d}{d\theta}e^{i\theta}=ie^{i\theta}$ ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) gives $\Phi_\theta=(ru',rv',0)=r(-v,u,0)$ and $\Phi_z=(0,0,1)$, so $\Phi_\theta\times\Phi_z=r(u,v,0)\ne0$ on $D^\circ$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the only seam is $\theta=0\leftrightarrow2\pi$ on the boundary, so $(D,\Phi)$ is an admissible regular surface patch ([[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]], [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]]). Since $E(\Phi(\theta,z))=\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}(u,v,0)$ and $u^2+v^2=|e^{i\theta}|^2=1$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]), the flux integrand of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]] is the constant $\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}$, and the patch integral equals $\frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0}\cdot\lambda_2(D)=\frac{\lambda L}{\varepsilon_0}$ ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).
For (d): the superposition identity $E(x)=\lambda\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{x-z e_3}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-z e_3|^3}\,dz$ is verified componentwise: $\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{dt}{(\rho^2+t^2)^{3/2}}=\frac{2}{\rho^2}$ and the third component is odd in $t$ with absolutely convergent integral zero; the whole $z$-integral is absolutely convergent because $\int_{\mathbb R}|x-z e_3|^{-2}dz=\pi/\rho$ and $x\mapsto|D\psi(x)|/\rho(x)$ is integrable for a compactly supported scalar or vector test: a bounding cylinder $\rho\le A$, $|x_3|\le H$ gives $\int 1/\rho\le(2H)2\pi A<\infty$ by transverse polar integration. The same estimate without $D\psi$ proves $E\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb R^3)$, and $\int\int|E_{1,z}(x)||D\psi(x)|dzdx\le(4\varepsilon_0)^{-1}\int|D\psi|/\rho<\infty$ proves absolute Fubini integrability. Here $E_{1,z}$ is the translated unit-charge field with the $\varepsilon_0$ normalization of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d); its value on its pole is immaterial ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). The pairing of the $z$-translated unit point-charge field with $\nabla\psi$ is $-\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\psi(0,0,z)$ by [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d); substituting into $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=-\int E\cdot\nabla\psi$ and interchanging by [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=\frac{\lambda}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(0,0,z)\,dz$ for every test function; the curl pairing with every vector test $\Psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ is $\int E\cdot\operatorname{curl}\Psi=\lambda\int dz\int E_{1,z}\cdot\operatorname{curl}\Psi=0$ by that same absolute majorant, since each translated unit-charge field has vanishing distributional curl ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).
For (e): the stated limits of $\varphi$ in $\rho$ and the effect of changing $r_0$ are the elementary properties of the logarithm ([[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]]); for the non-star-shapedness witness, given $a\in\Omega$ the point $-a$ lies in $\Omega$ and the segment $s\mapsto a+s(-a)=a(1-2s)$ passes through $0$ at $s=1/2$, which is on the excluded axis ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]).
For (f): $|E|^2=\frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2\rho^2}$, and the polar formula in the two transverse coordinates ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], $\sigma(S^1)=2\pi$ from $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$ with $|B_1|=\pi$ in the plane, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]) gives $\int_{\delta<\rho<R}\rho^{-2}\,d\lambda_2=2\pi\log(R/\delta)$; multiplying by the height $L$ and by $\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\cdot\frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2}$ yields the displayed identity, and $\log(R/\delta)\to\infty$ in either limit ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]] for the monotone convergence of the truncated integrals).
Clause (g) records the scope: [[def-em-weak-sources]] declares only point and stationary-sheet sources, so $\rho_\lambda$ is outside the framework's source types and the item makes no physical, equilibrium or empirical claim. For $\lambda=0$, both $E$ and $\varphi$ and $\rho_\lambda$ are zero, all fluxes and cutoff energies vanish, and the infinity normalization is available; the failure of that normalization and the two energy divergences concern only $\lambda\ne0$. The axis is null (a transverse singleton times bounded longitudinal intervals), so the zero extension does not alter regular distributions. The line-source functional is a distribution because on each compact test support its absolute pairing is at most $|\lambda|(2H)\|\psi\|_\infty$. The axis is contained in the coordinate hyperplane $x_1=0$, which is null by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]]. The translated unit-point field, with zero value at its pole, is jointly Borel in $(x,z)$; the scalar/vector-test products are Borel, and [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] with [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] supplies the product-measure identification for these Fubini calculations. The longitudinal integrals in (d) are evaluated first on finite intervals by [[thm-ftc-second-part]] and [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]: $t/(\rho^2\sqrt{\rho^2+t^2})$ is a primitive of $(\rho^2+t^2)^{-3/2}$, with limiting values $\pm1/\rho^2$; the third component is odd. Absolute convergence then passes to the full line. For the exact absolute-kernel majorant, evenness and the monotone substitution $t=\rho\sqrt{u/(1-u)}$ on $0<u<1$ give $\int_{\mathbb R}(\rho^2+t^2)^{-1}dt=\rho^{-1}B(1/2,1/2)=\pi/\rho$. The substitution has positive continuous derivative on compact truncations; [[thm-substitution-for-improper-integrals]] applies, with Riemann/Lebesgue comparison on those truncations and monotone convergence at the endpoints. The value follows from [[def-real-beta-integral]], [[thm-real-beta-gamma-identity]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]] and $\Gamma(1)=1$ in [[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]].

items.physical_scope: The idealised infinite straight line charge in vacuum: the field $\lambda\hat e_r/(2\pi\varepsilon_0\rho)$, the logarithmic potential, the zero-volume-source classical equations off the axis, the cylinder flux $\lambda L/\varepsilon_0$, the distributional identity $\operatorname{div}E=\rho_\lambda/\varepsilon_0$ on $\mathbb R^3$, the failure of the infinity normalization and of the star-shaped hypothesis, and the logarithmically divergent energy per unit length. The line source lies outside the declared source types of the framework; the item is a mathematical idealisation with no physical realisation, equilibrium or empirical claim.

items.title: The uniformly charged ball: interior and exterior fields, continuous potential and finite energy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $Q\in\mathbb R$, let $\overline B_a=\{x:|x|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and define, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]]),
$$\rho(x):=\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\,\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<a\}}(x),\qquad
E(x):=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\begin{cases}x/a^3,&|x|<a,\\ x/|x|^3,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad
\varphi(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{Q(3a^2-|x|^2)}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3},&|x|\le a,\\[6pt]\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|},&|x|\ge a.\end{cases}$$
(The value of $\rho$ on the sphere $\{|x|=a\}$ is immaterial: it is a Lebesgue-null set by the polar calculation $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$, since the one-dimensional singleton has measure zero ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]).) Then:
(a) [Regularity and gradient] $E$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$, of class $C^\infty$ on each of the open regions $\{|x|<a\}$, $\{|x|>a\}$; $\varphi\in C^1(\mathbb R^3)$, its displayed branch derivatives agree on $\{|x|=a\}$, and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]);
(b) [Classical equations] for every $x$ with $|x|\ne a$,
$$\operatorname{div}E(x)=\rho(x)/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E(x)=0$$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]);
(c) [Weak equations] the pair $(E,(\rho,0))$ satisfies the spatial distributional equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$: $E$ is $C^1$ on each side of the sphere $S_a=\{|x|=a\}$ with one-sided continuous traces that agree, $[E]=0$, so [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=\{\operatorname{curl}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=0,$$
with $\rho$ the displayed locally integrable density and no surface-charge term ([[def-em-weak-sources]], [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]] for the sphere as a compact embedded smooth hypersurface); by the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) these are the weak equations of the static model for this source, with zero singular part;
(d) [Energy] the field energy is finite and equals the assembly integral,
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a},$$
computed with the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]); the value agrees with the smooth-source identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] although the density here is only piecewise continuous;
(e) [Consistency and contrast] for $|x|>a$ the field is exactly the point-charge Coulomb field of total charge $Q$ centred at the origin ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $x_0=0$) although the source is the extended ball, and for $|x|<a$ it is the affine field $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ and decays at infinity; the field is bounded on $\mathbb R^3$, so no divergence of field energy occurs for the extended source;
(f) [Scope] the example verifies the displayed candidate and its energy; it does not claim uniqueness of the solution (this would require boundary data and an infinity condition, and the density is not continuous), it asserts no empirical content, and the density $\rho$ is treated as a bounded $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ density with the sphere carrying no surface charge ($[E]=0$).
items.strategy:
For (a): on $\{|x|<a\}$, $E$ is the affine map $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and on $\{|x|>a\}$ it is $Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$; both are $C^\infty$ on their open domains ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). At $|x|=a$ the two formulas coincide ($x/a^3=x/a^3$), so $E$ is continuous on all of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]], [[def-metric-ball]]). For $\varphi$, the interior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)$ and the exterior branch has gradient $-Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3)$ by the chain rule, and the two gradients agree on $\{|x|=a\}$; the matching derivatives also exist on the interface, as follows. Let $F(r)$ be the displayed radial potential profile on $r\ge0$. Its two branches agree at $a$, and their one-sided derivatives both equal $-Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$, so the difference quotient $(F(a+h)-F(a))/h$ has that common limit from either sign. Thus $F$ is differentiable at $a$, and its derivative is continuous there by the branch formulas. Since $x\mapsto|x|$ is differentiable near each point of $S_a$, the chain rule proves actual total differentiability of $\varphi=F(|x|)$ there and gives the matching gradient. At the origin the interior polynomial already gives smoothness. The resulting partial derivatives exist and are continuous everywhere, whence $\varphi$ is $C^1$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
For (b): inside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3))=3Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3)=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and the curl of an affine field vanishes ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); outside, $\operatorname{div}(Qx/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^3))=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_i\partial_i(x_i|x|^{-3})=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}(3|x|^{-3}-3|x|^{-3})=0$ and the curl components $\partial_j(x_k|x|^{-3})-\partial_k(x_j|x|^{-3})=0$ vanish by the same direct differentiation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), matching $\rho=0$ outside.
For (c): the set $S_a$ is a compact embedded smooth hypersurface with unit normal $n=x/|x|$, and the two sides $\Omega_-=\{|x|<a\}$, $\Omega_+=\{|x|>a\}$ are open; $E$ is $C^1$ on each side and its one-sided traces agree on $S_a$ (from (a)), so $[E]=F_+-F_-=0$ in the notation of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies: the distributional divergence is the piecewise classical divergence plus $n\cdot[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$, and the distributional curl is the piecewise classical curl plus $n\times[E]\delta_{S_a}=0$. By (b) the piecewise divergence is $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ as a locally integrable function and the piecewise curl is $0$; the sphere is null by applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to its Borel indicator: $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$. A singleton is contained in intervals of arbitrarily small length, so its one-dimensional measure is zero; [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] then applies, and the pairing conventions are those of [[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. The static reading is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e), and the source objects are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]] with zero singular part.
For (d): by the polar formula and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]) one has $\int_{B_a}|x|^2\,d\lambda_3=4\pi\int_0^ar^4\,dr=\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}$ and $\int_{B_a}d\lambda_3=\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}$; hence
$$\int_{B_a}|E|^2=\Bigl(\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\Bigr)^2\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}=\frac{Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},\qquad \int_{|x|>a}|E|^2=\frac{Q^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2}\cdot 4\pi\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=\frac{Q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0^2a},$$
using $\int_a^\infty r^{-2}dr=1/a$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]] and monotone convergence, [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); the sum times $\varepsilon_0/2$ is $\frac{Q^2}{40\pi\varepsilon_0a}+\frac{Q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a}=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$. The assembly integral is computed from the same two radial integrals, $\frac12\int\rho\varphi=\frac12\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\frac{Q}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3}\bigl(3a^2\frac{4\pi a^3}{3}-\frac{4\pi a^5}{5}\bigr)=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a}$, so the identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] extends to this piecewise-continuous bounded density by direct verification; the density is bounded with compact support and all integrands are continuous off a null sphere ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]).
For (e): the exterior branch equals the formula of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (d) with $q=Q$, $x_0=0$; $\varphi$ is continuous at $|x|=a$ since both branches give $Q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a)$, and decays like $1/|x|$; $|E|\le |Q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0a^2)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, so the energy of (d) is finite and no point singularity arises. For (f): no uniqueness or empirical statement is used anywhere; the sphere's zero jump is exactly the checked equality of the two branches on $\{|x|=a\}$. The one-dimensional singleton used in the polar null-sphere calculation is null by [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]]. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.

items.physical_scope: The uniformly charged ball of radius $a$ and total charge $Q$ in vacuum: the candidate piecewise field and continuous potential, the pointwise and distributional static equations with the piecewise-constant density and zero surface charge, the exterior Coulomb field of total charge $Q$, the vanishing jump of the normal field, and the finite energy $3Q^2/(20\pi\varepsilon_0a)$ equal to the assembly integral. items.title: The boundary of a bounded smooth domain is a compact embedded hypersurface
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the boundary-chart and surface-measure interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]); no other choice principle is used. Let $k\ge1$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^k$ domain in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] (nonempty, bounded, open, and locally exactly the one-sided subgraph of a $C^k$ graph function over a hyperplane). Then:
(a) [Compactness and finiteness] $\partial D$ is nonempty and compact; the complement $\mathbb R^3\setminus\partial D$ need not be connected here. Moreover $\partial D$ has finitely many connected components, and each connected component of $\partial D$ is compact.
(b) [Finite embedded presentation] the local boundary charts give finitely many regular injective $C^k$ parametrisations of $\partial D$ with $C^k$ coordinate transitions, of the graph type required by [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]: writing a chart as $R(p)=(y,s)$, the graph map $y\mapsto R^{-1}(y,h(y))$ is injective, of class $C^k$, with $C^k$ inverse (the inverse is $p\mapsto\pi(R(p))$ restricted to the graph, where $\pi(y,s)=y$); consequently $\partial D$ is a compact embedded $C^k$ hypersurface, and for $k\ge1$ it carries the finite surface measure of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]].
(c) [Normal field] the outward unit normal $\nu$ of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]] is a continuous unit normal field on $\partial D$, with $\nu(x)$ orthogonal to the tangent plane of the graph chart at each $x$; it is the field used by the Green and divergence items cited by this page's consumers.
The statement is geometric: it asserts no differentiability of $D$ beyond $C^k$, no boundedness of chart derivatives beyond the compact patches, and no connectedness of either $D$ or $\partial D$.
items.strategy: The boundary is nonempty: otherwise the nonempty open bounded $D$ would also be closed and disconnect connected $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]], [[cor-rn-is-polygonally-connected-and-locally-path-connected]], [[thm-path-connected-implies-connected]]). It is closed and bounded, hence compact by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]. At every boundary point first shrink its graph chart to the inverse image of a small flattening cylinder $B'\times(-b,b)$ with $\overline{B'}$ compactly contained in the original parameter ball. Its boundary patch is exactly the graph $X(y)=R^{-1}(y,h(y))$ over the connected ball $B'$. The graph is homeomorphic to $B'$ by the coordinate projection, so is a connected relatively open neighbourhood in $\partial D$. Arbitrarily small such graph neighbourhoods prove local connectedness of $\partial D$ directly; local connectedness is not inherited by arbitrary Euclidean subspaces. A component is open because each of these connected neighbourhoods meeting it lies in it by maximality; it is closed because the closure of a connected set is connected (if separated, the two relative open separating sets would also separate the dense original connected set). Compactness and the open component cover therefore give finitely many components, each closed and compact. For the embedded presentation, the graph maps are injective and $C^k$, and their derivatives have independent tangent columns since projection onto $y$ has derivative the identity; their inverses are the restricted coordinate projections. Transitions are the corresponding projections composed with the graph maps and rigid motions, hence $C^k$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Choose these smaller chart neighbourhoods at every point first, and only then take a finite subcover of the compact boundary. The associated larger charts provide room for compact supports of a subordinate partition; their graph densities and derivatives are bounded on those compact supports. This supplies exactly the finite compact embedded hypersurface and finite surface measure of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The outward graph normal is the continuous $(-Dh,1)/\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$ transported by the rigid coordinates; overlap agreement is supplied by [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. No domain or boundary connectedness is assumed, and the only choice assumption used is the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

items.title: The vacuum region around compact smooth conductors is a bounded smooth domain
items.strategy: Let $K=\bigcup_j\overline D_j$. It is compact, contained in open $\Omega$, and its constituent closures are pairwise disjoint. For $m=0$, $K=\varnothing$. Thus $\Omega_v=\Omega\setminus K$ is open and bounded. It is nonempty: choose a boundary point of nonempty bounded $\Omega$ by [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]; a small neighbourhood of that point avoids compact $K$ and contains interior points of $\Omega$. At an outer boundary point shrink the $\Omega$ graph cylinder to avoid $K$; locally the vacuum is the same subgraph as $\Omega$. At a point of $\partial D_j$ shrink the $D_j$ chart cylinder to lie inside $\Omega$ and avoid every other closed body. Precisely $\Omega_v\cap W=W\setminus\overline D_j$, not $W\setminus D_j$: in graph coordinates its inequality is strictly $s>h(y)$. Reflection $w=-s$ makes this the subgraph $w<-h(y)$ with $C^k$ graph. These local charts also show $\partial\Omega_v=\partial\Omega\sqcup\bigsqcup_j\partial D_j$, since the disjoint compact closures prevent other bodies from hiding or touching any boundary piece. The outward normal is the outer-domain normal on $\partial\Omega$, and its negative on $\partial D_j$, because the latter vacuum chart is the exterior of the body. The graph-normal formula in [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]] verifies this sign. All boundary pieces are compact smooth hypersurfaces by [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]. For components, every point of the open vacuum has a connected open ball inside it; hence its connected component is open. Every boundary point of a component lies on $\partial\Omega_v$: a connected ball inside $\Omega_v$ cannot meet two components. Choose a small flattened cylinder at such a boundary point whose vacuum half-cylinder is connected. Because that half-cylinder meets the component, all of it lies in the component; its graph is therefore the component's local boundary. Thus the component is a bounded $C^k$ domain with the inherited normal on the restricted boundary. A finite cover of compact $\partial\Omega_v$ by such connected one-sided graph cylinders meets only finitely many vacuum components. Every nonempty bounded open component has a boundary point, so there are only finitely many components. A boundary component of $\Omega_v$ is incident to a single vacuum component: the incident component is locally constant along each connected graph boundary patch, hence constant along that boundary component. Consequently each $\partial U$ is a union of the incident compact boundary components, not necessarily the entire displayed disjoint union. None of these conclusions asserts vacuum connectedness. The corrected separation hypothesis excludes tangent bodies: two tangent balls have disjoint open interiors but a touching point of their closures does not admit the asserted disjoint single-boundary chart.

items.title: Uniqueness for harmonic functions on a punctured half-space with zero trace, decaying at the pole and at infinity
items.strategy: Fix $y\in H\setminus\{p\}$ and $\eta>0$. Choose $R>\max(2a,|y|)$ large enough that $|w|\le\eta$ on $H\cap\{|x|\ge R\}$, enlarging the decay threshold slightly; choose $0<\delta<\min(a/2,|y-p|,R-|p|)$ so small that $|w(x)|\le\eta/|x-p|$ whenever $0<|x-p|\le\delta$. On the nonempty bounded open $U=(B_R(0)\setminus\overline B_\delta(p))\cap H$, the functions $\pm w-\eta-\eta/|x-p|$ are harmonic and continuous on $\overline U$: the barrier $|x-p|^{-1}$ is harmonic off its pole by [[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]. On the plane they are nonpositive because $w=0$; on the outer sphere they are nonpositive by decay; on the inner sphere they are nonpositive by the sub-Coulomb pole condition. The weak maximum principle [[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]] therefore gives $|w(y)|\le\eta(1+|y-p|^{-1})$. Let $\eta\downarrow0$ with $y$ fixed to obtain $w(y)=0$. This proves uniqueness for all sub-Coulomb remainders, including arbitrary bounded remainders and the earlier zero-remainder-limit class, without a removable-singularity theorem or extra boundary smoothness assumption.

items.title: The ideal electrostatic conductor model
items.statement:
Under the Countable Choice convention of the stated boundary and sheet-distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), Adopt as a physical model of ideal electrostatic conductors, for the classical laboratory framework of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: a **conductor configuration** consists of the following data, and every model of this postulate is required to satisfy the clauses below. No experiment is reported and no empirical value is inferred; this is an explicitly adopted equilibrium idealization together with its geometric and source conventions.
(a) [Geometry] a laboratory region $\Omega\times I$ with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ an arbitrary open ambient region, a finite family $D_1,\dots,D_m$ ($m\ge1$) of bounded $C^\infty$ domains with pairwise disjoint closures in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with closures strictly inside $\Omega$ (the **conductor bodies**), the **conductor** $D:=D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_m$, its **surface** $\partial D$, and the **vacuum region** $\Omega_v:=\Omega\setminus\overline D$. By [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]], $\partial D=\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$ is a disjoint union of compact embedded $C^\infty$ hypersurfaces. The vacuum $\Omega_v$ is open, and near each conductor surface it is locally the smooth exterior side of that conductor. No boundedness or regularity of the ambient boundary is inferred from openness. In the additional **bounded smooth ambient branch**, assume that $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain; only then [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] gives that $\Omega_v$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with the specified outer/conductor boundary charts; we additionally require $\Omega_v$ to be connected (configurations whose vacuum region is separated by the conductors, for instance by an enclosing closed shell, are outside this model as formulated here).
(b) [Equilibrium and sources] the configuration is in the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] on the vacuum region: $B=0$, $J=0$, $E$ is the fixed-time electric field of [[def-em-fields]], the volume source density $\rho_v$ is a continuous real map on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (C m$^{-3}$, [[def-em-sources]]) extended by zero to $D$; the **conductor charge is a stationary surface charge**, i.e. a continuous density $\sigma:\partial D\to\mathbb R$ (C m$^{-2}$) whose pairing with test functions is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with tangential current $K=0$ and $S=\partial D$; and the field pair $(E,0)$ together with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\ 0)$ satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]. Inside the conductor the field vanishes: $E\equiv0$ on $D$ (the **equilibrium condition**); equivalently the conductor interior is field-free and carries no volume charge.
(c) [Potential and equipotential convention] there is a function $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and with $\varphi$ constant on each conductor body, $\varphi|_{D_j}\equiv V_j$ for real constants $V_j$ (volts, [[def-em-si-conventions]]); by continuity of $\varphi$ the trace of $\varphi$ on each $\partial D_j$ from the vacuum side equals $V_j$ as well. This is the single-function convention of an ideal conductor with no double layer: the model reads the same potential value on both sides of $\partial D$, while the normal component of $E$ may jump.
(d) [Data] a model is completed either by the component potentials $V_1,\dots,V_m$ together with the volume source $\rho_v$ and the data on $\partial\Omega$ where the laboratory region is bounded, or by the component total charges $Q_j:=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS$ (C) together with those same ambient data. These are two declared data types; the postulate asserts neither that both data types are simultaneously specifiable nor that either is solvable for arbitrary data.
(e) [Scope] This is a static, frame-relative equilibrium idealization: it excludes transient finite-conductivity dynamics, relaxation to equilibrium, moving surface charge, electrode polarization and contact effects, and it is not derived from a microscopic matter model. It asserts no existence or uniqueness theorem (those are separate conditional results), no force, no energy, no radiation, no measurement and no apparatus realization; the value $V_j$ is a model parameter and the surface density $\sigma$ is an idealization variable determined by the equilibrium problem when it is solvable. The general open ambient branch retains compact conductor bodies in exterior configurations. Its additional bounded smooth ambient branch is distinct from the separately declared grounded-half-space and infinite parallel-plane idealizations, whose conductor bodies are themselves noncompact. Those examples retain the equilibrium/equipotential interpretation but their noncompact bodies and plane distributions are not instances of this compact-body configuration or its compact-sheet predicate. No arbitrary exterior solvability is asserted.
items.strategy: Nonproof formulation and scope review: adopt the equilibrium objects already defined in the framework and record their exact interfaces instead of proving a physical law. Textbook conductor treatments support each clause as a model choice: the vanishing interior field with all charge on the surface and the constant potential of an equipotential conductor ([[def-em-weak-sources]]'s stationary-sheet source is the framework's own surface-distribution object), the grounded/fixed-potential and fixed-charge data distinction, and the idealization's limits are stated rather than hidden. The mathematical identities used to name the objects are exact: $\partial D$ is a finite disjoint union of compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces by [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]. For general open $\Omega$, removing the finite compact separated closures gives an open vacuum, with smooth local exterior conductor charts because each compact body is strictly inside $\Omega$ and separated from the others. The vacuum need not be bounded or have a smooth outer boundary. Only under the additionally imposed bounded $C^\infty$ ambient hypothesis does [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]] give a bounded smooth vacuum; the surface pairing $\sigma\delta_{\partial D}$ is the one of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) under the surface-distribution conventions of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and carries its declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the field, source and regime objects are those of [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]; and the adopted solution predicate is [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not a consequence of the smooth postulate. The clause (d) data distinction is a definitional choice (Dirichlet data $V_j$ versus charge data $Q_j$), and clause (e) states the exclusions; in particular no claim is made that a configuration exists for arbitrary data, and no empirical or metrological content is attached to the idealization.

items.physical_scope: The ideal electrostatic conductor idealization of the classical framework in one named inertial frame: finitely many compact smooth field-free conductor bodies inside a general open laboratory region, with a separate bounded smooth ambient branch, all conductor charge carried by continuous stationary surface densities, a connected vacuum region in which the pure electrostatic regime and the adopted distributional Maxwell equations hold, and a continuous equilibrium potential that is constant on each conductor body and continuous across its surface. The item is a model choice: it asserts no existence, uniqueness, dynamics, conductivity, forces, energy, radiation, measurement or apparatus claim, and it excludes cavity configurations with disconnected vacuum regions.

items.title: Surface charge and normal field on an ideal conductor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the surface and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v;E;\rho_v;\sigma;V_j)$ be a model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with surface $S:=\partial D$ and vacuum region $\Omega_v$, with the fields of [[def-em-fields]], the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] carried by the model, and suppose additionally that the field $E$ satisfies the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] across $S$: around every $x_0\in S$ each side of $S$ is the restriction of a $C^1$ field on an open neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller graph chart. Let $n$ denote the unit normal on $S$ pointing from the conductor side into the vacuum side (equivalently: $n$ is the inward normal of $\Omega_v$ and the outward normal of $D$ on $S$, by the local exterior conductor chart; in the bounded smooth ambient branch this is the sign convention of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)), and let $E_+$ denote the vacuum-side trace of $E$ (the field is zero on the conductor side, so $[E]=E_+$). Then, pointwise on $S$:
(a) [Normal sheet charge] $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n\times E_+=0$; equivalently $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$ and the tangential part of the vacuum-side field vanishes: $E_+$ has no component tangent to $S$. In particular a conductor surface with $\sigma=0$ at a point has $E_+=0$ there (both traces vanish), and the sign of $\sigma$ is the sign of the outward normal field component.
(b) [Normal derivative of the potential] with $\varphi$ the model's potential and $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ the one-sided normal derivative in the direction $n$ from the conductor into the vacuum ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), one has
$$\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}=-\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sigma=-\varepsilon_0\,\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}.$$
(c) [Equipotential boundary traces] the trace $\varphi_+$ of $\varphi$ on $S$ is constant on each connected component of $S$, with value $V_j$ on every connected component contained in $\partial D_j$; consequently the boundary value problem in the vacuum region is a Dirichlet problem whose data are the constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces.
(d) [Total charges] the total charge of conductor $j$ is
$$Q_j=\int_{\partial D_j}\sigma\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\nu}\,dS,$$
where $\nu$ is the local outward normal of the vacuum along the smooth conductor interface $S$, without asserting regularity of a general ambient outer boundary (so $\nu=-n$ on $\partial D$ and the last equality uses $\partial\varphi/\partial\nu=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$); the surface integrals exist as integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]).
(e) [Data reading] the two data types of the model are related through (d): if the component potentials and ambient data are fixed and the equilibrium solution is given, the total charges are determined by (d); prescribing the total charges instead determines the potentials only through the (separate) equilibrium problem, and this theorem asserts no existence or uniqueness for charge data.
(f) [Scope] The statement is pointwise and stationary: it assumes the one-sided joint regularity above, a $C^\infty$ conductor surface, and the pure electrostatic regime; it excludes moving surface charge, normal sheet currents, magnetic sheet sources, nonsmooth or cornered conductors, fields without one-sided traces, forces, energy and any measurement; no self-force or material response is asserted.
items.strategy:
The model supplies $E\equiv0$ on the conductor side and the source pair $(ho_v+\sigma\delta_S,0)$ with $K=0$ as the stationary-sheet pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] supplies the adopted weak Maxwell equations; the joint one-sided regularity is the hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. Applying that theorem with $\Omega_-$ the conductor side, $\Omega_+$ the vacuum side and the chosen normal $n$ (its sign convention is exactly the one of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] fixed in the model) gives, pointwise on $S$, $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n	imes[E]=0$ together with the two magnetic identities. Since $E\equiv0$ on the conductor side, $[E]=E_+-0=E_+$, proving (a) and the formula $\sigma=\varepsilon_0n\cdot E_+$. For (b): on the vacuum side $E=-
abla\varphi$ by the model, and $\varphi$ is $C^2$ in the vacuum interior, is continuous on $S$, and its gradient has the continuous one-sided trace $-E_+$ by the admitted field regularity; the parallel-graph derivative argument below identifies the actual tangential derivatives of the trace; hence $n\cdot E_+=-n\cdot
abla\varphi_+=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$ with the classical normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]], and substituting into (a) gives the stated sign. For (c): $n	imes E_+=0$ says precisely that all tangential first derivatives of $\varphi_+$ vanish at every point of $S$; the trace $t\mapsto\varphi_+(t)$ is therefore locally constant on the embedded hypersurface $S$, and a locally constant continuous function on a connected component is constant there ([[def-connected-component-and-quasicomponent]]; in each graph chart the trace has zero gradient, so [[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]] makes it constant on the chart, and local constancy on a connected set gives constancy on the whole component). On a component contained in $\partial D_j$ the model's continuity convention gives the value $V_j$ ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]](c)). For (d): the total charge is the surface integral of $\sigma$, which exists because $\sigma$ is continuous on the compact $S$ and the surface measure is finite ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-boundary-of-a-bounded-smooth-domain-is-a-compact-embedded-hypersurface]]); substituting (a) gives the middle expression, and the last equality is $
u=-n$ and $\partial\varphi/\partial
u=
abla\varphi_+\cdot
u=-
abla\varphi_+\cdot n=-\partial\varphi/\partial n$, with the local exterior-side vacuum normal, agreeing with [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c) whenever its additional bounded ambient hypothesis holds. No product of distributions is formed, no equation at a corner is asserted, and the result is exactly the pointwise form of the conductor boundary condition under the stated regularity. The potential's gradient trace needed in (b)-(c) is justified by the field trace: $
abla\varphi=-E$ in the vacuum, so its first derivatives extend continuously to the boundary by $-E_+$. In a graph chart, restrict $\varphi$ to parallel graphs inside the vacuum. On a compact coordinate segment their derivatives are $-E\cdot\partial_yX_s$ and converge uniformly to $-E_+\cdot\partial_yX_0$ as $s\downarrow0$; the functions converge to the continuous boundary trace. [[thm-uniform-derivative-limit-on-a-closed-interval]] proves that this is the actual derivative of the trace, so constancy of the trace and tangential-field cancellation are legitimate without assuming an unprovided ambient extension of the potential.

items.physical_scope: The ideal-conductor boundary conditions of classical electrostatics in a named inertial frame: for a stationary smooth conductor surface in the pure electrostatic regime and fields with the stated one-sided regularity, the surface charge density equals epsilon_0 times the normal vacuum-side field, the vacuum-side field is normal to the surface, the potential trace is constant on each connected piece of the conductor surface with the model's component value, and the total component charges are the outward flux integrals of the vacuum field. The statement is conditional and pointwise; it excludes moving or nonsmooth surfaces, magnetic and current sources, forces, energy, material response and any empirical claim.

items.title: Uniqueness and flux compatibility for the electrostatic boundary value problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited weak-solvability and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (the fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be real potentials of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields $E_i:=-\nabla\varphi_i$ of [[def-em-fields]] and
$$-\Delta\varphi_i=\rho/\varepsilon_0\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega_v,\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla.$$ The Laplacian convention is [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
Let $\nu$ denote the outward unit normal of $\Omega_v$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]). Then:
(a) [Classical Dirichlet uniqueness] if $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and hence $E_1=E_2$. The conclusion holds component by component; each connected component of a bounded $C^\infty$ domain is again a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, to which the connected-domain uniqueness corollary applies.
(b) [Classical Neumann uniqueness and compatibility] if $\partial_\nu\varphi_1=\partial_\nu\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ is constant on each connected component of $\Omega_v$, and conversely adding one real constant per component to a solution preserves both the equation and the Neumann data; hence the field $E$ is unique while the potential is determined only up to componentwise constants. Moreover the Neumann data are necessarily compatible:
$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}.$$
This compatibility is necessary, not sufficient, and is exactly the flux identity of the divergence theorem for the Poisson equation.
(c) [Weak variants] (i) if $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_v)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]) is prescribed as a trace and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ are weak solutions of the Dirichlet problem with the same trace $g$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$; (ii) if the conormal data are prescribed compatibly, weak $H^1$ solutions are unique modulo constants on each connected component, and for connected $\Omega_v$ this is the normalised solution of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; (iii) [sheet/transmission variant] for the finite disjoint smooth interfaces and outer Dirichlet data of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c), the globally $H^1$ solution is unique, and for compatible outer Neumann data it is unique modulo componentwise constants until the componentwise means are fixed.
(d) [Physics reading and conductor case] on a star-shaped vacuum domain the curl-free $C^1$ field has an interior $C^2$ potential by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]. This alone does not supply closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace, or prescribed boundary data; each application of (a)-(c) additionally requires its stated regularity and identical boundary/source data. In the bounded conductor model, prescribed absolute conductor potentials $V_j$ and absolute outer Dirichlet data determine the potential and field uniquely in the admitted classical or weak class. Grounding fixes the additive constant exactly. If only relative potential differences are prescribed and the outer/reference data are also allowed to shift by the same constant, the common gauge constant is free; merely omitting outer boundary data does not establish field uniqueness.
(e) [Scope] uniqueness is conditional on the stated boundary or decay data: on an unbounded exterior region without a decay condition uniqueness fails: on $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ the functions $0$ and $u(x)=1-R/|x|$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity (the witness is verified in the strategy), so the boundary, decay and regularity hypotheses above cannot be dropped. No existence is inferred from uniqueness; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric material coefficient or empirical claim is included. For the admitted conductor class with connected vacuum, fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Neumann data also give exact uniqueness: this is a mixed boundary problem with a nonempty Dirichlet part, so there is no surviving additive constant. Existence for those mixed data is not asserted here. In that weak mixed branch, write $\mathcal V_D=\{v\in H^1(\Omega_v):Tv=0\text{ on }\partial D\}$. The compared potentials have the same prescribed conductor trace and satisfy $\varepsilon_0\int_{\Omega_v}\nabla v\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for every $v\in\mathcal V_D$, with the same smooth outer normal datum $g$.
items.strategy:
All four statements are read off their suppliers, with the physics conventions made explicit. (a) On each connected component $U$ of $\Omega_v$, the restricted potentials are $C^2(\overline U)$ with equal Laplacians $ho/\varepsilon_0$ and equal boundary traces, so the classical Dirichlet corollary ([[cor-classical-dirichlet-and-poisson-problems-are-unique]] claim 1) gives equality on $\overline U$; components are bounded by [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] and inherit the smooth-domain property as in [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](d). The fields then agree because $E_i=-
abla\varphi_i$ and the gradient is determined by the potential. (b) The same corollary's second claim ([[cor-neumann-solutions-are-unique-modulo-componentwise-constants]]) gives constancy of $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ on each component from equal normal derivatives. The compatibility identity is [[lem-neumann-compatibility-from-the-divergence-theorem]] applied to $u=\varphi$, $f=-\Delta\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $g=\partial_
u\varphi$; its conclusion $\int f=-\int g$ is the displayed equation, and the source notes of that lemma record that it is necessary rather than sufficient. (c) (i) is the uniqueness clause of [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]] (the weak solution with prescribed trace is exactly one); (ii) is the uniqueness-modulo-constants and normalisation clause of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]] with the trace spaces of [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]; (iii) is [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c) verbatim in its uniqueness clause: outer Dirichlet data give the globally $H^1$ solution uniquely, outer compatible Neumann data give uniqueness modulo componentwise constants until the means are fixed. (d) The radial Poincare construction provides $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega_v)$ in the interior only. Before invoking (a), require the asserted continuous derivatives through order two on the closure and matching classical traces; before invoking (c), require $H^1$ membership, the specified trace/conormal problem, and matching weak right-hand sides. These are independent data/regularity hypotheses. Under the conductor Dirichlet data, the differences of admitted solutions have zero trace on every conductor and the prescribed outer boundary, so (a) or (c)(i) gives zero difference, not an unfixed constant. A common gauge shift preserves a relative-potential problem only when every reference datum is shifted as well. (e) For the failure of uniqueness on unbounded regions, put $\Omega_R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|>R\}$ and $u(x):=1-R/|x|$; then $u\in C^\infty(\Omega_R)$, $u=0$ on $\{|x|=R\}$, $0<u<1$ on $\Omega_R$ and $u(x)	o1$ as $|x|	o\infty$, while $\Delta u=0$ because $R/|x|$ is the constant $4\pi R$ times the $n=3$ fundamental solution, harmonic off the origin ([[lem-laplace-fundamental-solution-is-harmonic-off-its-pole]]) with the constant multiple and the constant function having zero Laplacian by linearity ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); hence $0$ and $u$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, so the boundary/decay hypotheses in (a)-(c) cannot be dropped. No existence statement is made anywhere: the existence clauses are the separate declared existence result of this page and the cited weak-solvability lemmas, and the compatibility identity is used only in its necessary direction. For the mixed conductor data mentioned in (d), let $w$ be the difference of two admitted solutions. It is harmonic, $w=0$ on the conductor boundary and $\partial_
u w=0$ on the outer boundary. Green's first identity gives $\int_{\Omega_v}|
abla w|^2=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}w\partial_
u w=0$ because each boundary piece has one zero factor. Thus $w$ is constant on the connected vacuum and its zero trace on the nonempty conductor boundary makes that constant zero. For admitted weak mixed solutions, their difference has zero conductor trace, is an admissible test of the homogeneous mixed difference equation, and the same zero-energy argument applies. This conditional uniqueness requires the displayed boundary/trace class and does not supply a mixed existence theorem. In the weak mixed case the mean-zero inequality [[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]] turns $
abla w=0$ into $w=w_{\Omega_v}$ as an $H^1$ class. Its constant trace on the nonempty conductor boundary is zero, so the constant is zero; no classical differentiability of a general $H^1$ representative is assumed.

items.physical_scope: Uniqueness for the classical and weak Dirichlet/Neumann electrostatic boundary value problems in a bounded vacuum region of a named inertial frame, with the componentwise Neumann freedom, the necessary flux compatibility, and the conductor-potential reading: identical complete Dirichlet data determine the potential and field exactly; compatible Neumann data determine the field and leave one potential constant per connected component until a normalization is fixed. The statement is conditional on the stated boundary, decay and regularity data and on the cited mathematical suppliers; it asserts no existence, no arbitrary-boundary solvability, no material interfaces beyond the declared sheet branch, and no empirical claim.

items.title: Existence and regularity for the electrostatic boundary value problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited solvability theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]) and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be the framework constant. Then the electrostatic boundary value problems on $\Omega_v$ are solvable in the following exact senses, and the solutions are the fields of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with volume source $\rho$:
(a) [Dirichlet branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ there is exactly one $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with
$$-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0\quad\text{on }\Omega_v,\qquad \varphi|_{\partial\Omega_v}=g,$$
with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]];
and it is the unique weak $H^1$ solution with trace $g$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the class); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ ([[def-em-fields]]) is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and $(E,0)$ realises the pure electrostatic regime with source $\rho$ on the vacuum region.
(b) [Neumann branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ with
$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}g\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}\text{ of }\Omega_v,$$
there is $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ (outward normal $\nu$, [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), unique up to one additive constant per connected component; the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\varphi\,dx=0$ for every $j$ selects exactly one. The compatibility is also necessary in the sense of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b).
(c) [Conductor reading and surface-charge realization] for the separated compact-body conductor geometry and zero-interior-volume convention of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally assuming $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain, with outer boundary data $g_0\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ on $\partial\Omega$ and constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces $\partial D_j$ (constant functions are smooth on the compact disjoint boundary pieces), the combined datum is a special case of (a); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ extended by $E:=0$ on the conductor satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\,0)$, where $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$ is the constructed continuous surface-charge density, agreeing afterwards with [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] ([[def-em-weak-sources]](c), [[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]); the total charges $Q_j=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]) are thereby determined by the data, and $\varphi$ is constant on each $\partial D_j$ with value $V_j$.
(d) [Stationary sheet charge in the vacuum region] for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces $\Gamma$ strictly inside $\Omega_v$, a smooth sheet density $\sigma_\Gamma$ on them, and outer Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$, there is a weak solution $\varphi\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ which is $C^\infty$ on the closure of each side of every $\Gamma$, unique by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](c)(iii), solving the weak equation with right-hand side $\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma\,Tv$; its flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=-\sigma_\Gamma$, equivalently $n\cdot[E]=\sigma_\Gamma/\varepsilon_0$ in the sign convention of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. This is the vacuum ($\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$) transmission branch; no dielectric coefficient is introduced.
(e) [Scope] all existence statements are the ones proved in [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] for its stated smooth bounded domains, smooth uniformly positive coefficients (here $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$), smooth data and finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces; the coefficient is the smooth positive constant $\varepsilon_0I$ on every side in the transmission clause. Excluded: nonsmooth boundaries, corners, edges, coefficient loss of regularity, prescribed total charges for conductor bodies (the free equipotential problem), unbounded exterior regions without a stated decay class, dielectric material response (belonging to the material-response page) and any measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The theorem asserts existence of the potential, not of a physical equilibrium; the ideal conductor is the adopted model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]].
items.strategy:
The conductor application in (c) explicitly uses the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch, not the general open ambient model. The proof is a careful application of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] to the vacuum geometry, combined with the framework's distributional reading.
(a) Take $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$, which is smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and uniformly positive; the theorem's clause (a) gives exactly one weak solution with trace $g$, $C^\infty$ on the closure, with $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon_0
abla\varphi)=-\varepsilon_0\Delta\varphi=ho$ pointwise and the prescribed boundary values. Dividing by $\varepsilon_0>0$ gives the displayed equation; the field $E=-
abla\varphi$ is $C^\infty$ with $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, so the static reduction of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](c) holds with $\partial_t=0$ and the pair $(E,0)$ is a pure electrostatic model. (b) The theorem's clause (b) with conormal datum $\varepsilon_0g$, since $
u\cdot\varepsilon_0
abla\varphi=\varepsilon_0\partial_
u\varphi=\varepsilon_0g$ gives a weak solution exactly under the displayed compatibility, unique modulo componentwise constants, normalised by the mean conditions; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure is the same clause. On each connected component, the weak identity tested with the constant $1$ reproduces the compatibility, matching [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b). (c) The datum that is $g_0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and $V_j$ on $\partial D_j$ is a function on the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v=\partial\Omega\sqcup\partial D$ restricting to a smooth function on each piece, hence smooth on the boundary manifold; clause (a) applies with this $g$ and gives $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=ho_v/\varepsilon_0$ (the volume source is $ho_v$). Define $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0 n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$; the solution has constant trace $V_j$ on $\partial D_j$ because it solves the Dirichlet problem. Extend the potential by the constant $V_j$ inside $D_j$; the resulting function is continuous across each boundary. The tangential derivatives of the vacuum trace are zero: pull back the smooth up-to-boundary solution to a boundary graph and use the chain rule (or the uniform derivative-limit argument for parallel interior graphs). Therefore $E_+\cdot	au=-\partial_	au\varphi=0$ for every tangent vector $	au$, and $n	imes E_+=0$ is derived directly from the boundary datum. The density is defined by the displayed normal trace, before using any theorem that assumes a completed conductor model. Extend the field by zero on $D$ and let $\widetilde E$ denote the extension; on the open sets $\Omega_v$ and $D$ it is respectively $C^\infty$ and zero, so it has $C^\infty$ one-sided traces across the compact embedded interface $\partial D$ with normal $n$, and [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives, distributionally, $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=\{\operatorname{div}\widetilde E\}_{	ext{piecewise}}+n\cdot[\widetilde E]\,\delta_{S}$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=\{\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E\}_{	ext{piecewise}}+n	imes[\widetilde E]\,\delta_S$ with $S=\partial D$. The piecewise divergence is $ho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on $\Omega_v$ and $0$ on $D$; the piecewise curl is zero on both sides; $[\widetilde E]=E_+$ and $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n	imes E_+=0$ by the constant-trace argument just proved. Hence $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=(ho_v+\sigma\delta_S)/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$, with the sheet pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) and the surface conventions of [[def-em-surface-distribution]]; together with $B=0$ and $J=0$ these are the four adopted equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] on the (time-independent) laboratory region, by the static dictionary of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]. The total charges follow by integrating the continuous density over the compact hypersurfaces ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). (d) This is [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c) with the constant coefficient $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$, piecewise smooth bulk data and smooth sheet charge; the equal one-sided traces, one-sided smoothness and the jump sign are as stated there, and the identification with the framework's jump convention is [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] ($n$ from the minus to the plus side). (e) records the exact hypotheses and the exclusions; no existence claim is made beyond the cited theorem, and in particular the free charge-data conductor problem and the exterior problem are left open. The extended potential, the zero interior field, the constructed sheet density and the verified distributional equations now satisfy the bounded conductor model; only after this construction may [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] be invoked as a consequence. For (d) the coefficient form is explicitly $\varepsilon_0\int
abla v\cdot
abla\varphi=\intho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma Tv$; hence bulk and sheet data are not multiplied by $\varepsilon_0$, whereas a prescribed outward normal datum $g$ corresponds to conormal datum $\varepsilon_0g$. Both the sheet jump and all source factors follow from this same form.
