It asserts nothing about any apparatus, no historical claim, no dataset, no sampling law and no probability; it is an exact algebraic nonidentifiability of the declared model.

items.title: An ideal electric-field zero and a declared detector-bin response
items.statement:
Adopt the two-beam data and conclusions of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]]:
for $v\in\mathbb C^3$ write $|v|^2:=\sum_{j=1}^3v_j\overline{v_j}
=\sum_{j=1}^3|v_j|^2$, using the scalar conjugation and modulus of
[[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this agrees with
the Euclidean squared norm on real vectors. Use
the complex electric amplitude $\alpha(x)=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ and
magnetic amplitude $\beta(x)=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ of its clause (a),
with $\delta(x)=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$, $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and the plane-wave solutions $(E_j,B_j)$ of
[[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]; and its clause (b) averaged energy density
$$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2$$
with the SI constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as
inherited by the Lebesgue-measure and integral items cited in clause (ii),
which are stated under that hypothesis; no other choice principle is used.
Assume dimensionless $a_1=a_2=:a>0$, $e_1=e_2=:e$ with real amplitude vector $e$, and
$k_1\ne k_2$ with $(k_2-k_1)\times e\ne0$; let $x_0$ be a point with
$\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}$.

(i) [Ideal prediction and its vanishing] At such $x_0$ one has
$\alpha(x_0)=ae(1+e^{i\delta(x_0)})=0$
([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]),
hence the electric field of the superposition vanishes at $x_0$ for every $t$
and the electric term of the averaged energy density vanishes there. The full
averaged energy density need not vanish:
$\beta(x_0)=a(b_1-b_2)=a\bigl((k_1-k_2)\times e\bigr)/\omega\ne0$, so
$\langle u\rangle(x_0)=|a(b_1-b_2)|^2/(4\mu_0)>0$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]] for the positive-definite norm). Thus a claim
that 'the ideal intensity vanishes at $x_0$' must name the quantity that
vanishes.

(ii) [Declared bin response and its finite-rate branch] Adopt a declared
detector model with a Lebesgue-measurable bin $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$,
$x_0\in W$ and $\lambda_3(W)>0$, a finite real response coefficient
$\kappa\ge0$, and a declared nonnegative density $b:W\to[0,\infty)$ whose zero
extension $\tilde b$ (equal to $b$ on $W$ and to $0$ off $W$) is Lebesgue
measurable; this measurability of the zero extension is a declared hypothesis
of the detector model. The declared response functional uses numerical values
in fixed declared units:
spatial coordinates are in metres, so $\lambda_3$ carries $\mathrm m^3$;
$\alpha$ carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ as in
[[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]. Fix a declared SI unit $\mathsf U$ of
accumulated response (possibly dimensionless); a response rate means response
per unit time, in $\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Declare $\kappa$ in
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm V^{-2}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $b$ (including
any constant $b_0$) in $\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Thus
$\kappa|\alpha|^2+b$ is a response-rate density in
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $R(W)$ carries
$\mathsf U\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. This is a declared response model, without an
empirical identification with a detector output. It is defined by the nonnegative
Lebesgue integral
$$R(W):=\int_W\bigl(\kappa|\alpha(x)|^2+b(x)\bigr)\,d\lambda_3\in[0,+\infty].$$
Here the continuous real function $|\alpha|^2$ is Borel measurable by
[[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]] and Lebesgue measurable by
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]; closure under nonnegative scaling
and addition is supplied by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]], and
[[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]] defines the extended integral. No
boundedness or finite-volume condition on $W$ is imposed. If
$\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$, monotonicity gives
$$R(W)\ge\int_W b\,d\lambda_3>0$$ even though $|\alpha(x_0)|^2=0$. For a
constant $b=b_0>0$ this lower bound is $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by
[[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]],
[[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]] and
[[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]; it may be
$+\infty$. The *finite predicted rate* branch additionally requires
$R(W)<\infty$, in the response-rate units just declared. A concrete sufficient case is
$0<\lambda_3(W)<\infty$ and constant $0<b_0<\infty$: the bound
$|\alpha|^2\le4a^2|e|^2$ gives
$$0<b_0\lambda_3(W)\le R(W)\le(4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0)\lambda_3(W)<\infty.$$
For $\kappa=0$ the field contribution is the zero function, without forming
$0\cdot(+\infty)$. Identifying a finite predicted response with a recorded
comparison quantity still requires the apparatus, calibration and analysis
declarations of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]]. Thus a finite positive
bin prediction is compatible with the ideal pointwise zero, but an extended
infinite response is not a recorded finite rate, and neither response is an
event probability.

(iii) [Record versus prediction; statistical qualification] The data of
[[def-em-experiment-record-contract]] are a finite tuple of real recorded
values or reported observations with declared conditions, calibration and
uncertainty. The predictions of (i)-(ii) are deterministic field quantities or
a declared extended response functional, with a finite real rate only on its
stated finite branch. Here an ideal fringe pattern describes spatial variation
of a specified intensity or response; a single detection and a finite data
tuple are separate records. Whether a finite record displays a specified
visibility or pattern requires a declared criterion, calibration, binning,
background and sampling assumptions, none supplied by the field calculation
alone. No sampling law, probability of failing a visibility criterion,
detection statistics or measured histogram is asserted. This example
discriminates no classical or quantum ontology: classical electromagnetic
waves interfere and the coherence calculation is a deterministic prediction of
the classical model.
items.strategy: Direct substitution and declared assumptions. (i): substitute the stated amplitude data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]]; at $\delta(x_0)\equiv\pi$ the factor $1+e^{i\pi}=0$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]), giving $\alpha(x_0)=0$ and vanishing electric field at $x_0$ for every $t$; the magnetic amplitude is $a(b_1-b_2)$ with $b_1-b_2=((k_1-k_2)\times e)/\omega\ne0$ by the bilinearity of the cross product ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and the nondegeneracy of the Euclidean norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), so the magnetic term of the averaged density is positive at $x_0$. (ii): $\alpha$ is a smooth plane-wave amplitude, so $|\alpha|^2$ is continuous. The cited continuous-to-Borel and Borel-to-Lebesgue suppliers, under the already stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, supply its measurability. Restrict to measurable $W$; the explicitly measurable $b$ extends by zero, with positive superlevels measurable in the ambient space. The closure supplier makes the nonnegative sum measurable. Monotonicity applies in $[0,+\infty]$ and proves the lower bound without finiteness. A positive constant background integrates to $b_0\lambda_3(W)$ by the simple-integral suppliers. In the finite-volume constant-background branch, $\alpha=ae(1+e^{i\delta})$ and the unit modulus of the exponential and subadditivity of its scalar complex modulus ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]) give $|\alpha|\le2a|e|$. Compare the entire integrand with the constant $4\kappa a^2|e|^2+b_0$ and use the same monotonicity and simple-integral formula for the finite upper bound; this uses no unproved integral additivity and handles $\kappa=0$ as the zero function. Unbounded or infinite-measure bins retain the extended response contract; only a separately verified finite response can enter the real-valued record vocabulary. (iii): the record structure is that of [[def-em-experiment-record-contract]], and the vanishing pointwise value is not by itself the bin response; no sampling model, probability, dataset or observation is introduced, and the classical-wave interference character of the prediction is that of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] clause (d). The only choice assumption is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, declared for the Lebesgue-measure and integral interface used in clause (ii); no other choice principle is used.

items.title: Smooth finite-region Maxwell action, compact variations and the fixed-endpoint particle functional
items.statement:
For the field sector (a)-(b), assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as inherited from [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]], whose functional and finiteness statement this item instantiates; the definition uses no further choice. The finite-interval Riemann particle sector (c) uses the choice-free curve lemma and does not require that field-sector measure convention. Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], with $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let worldlines be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]].

(a) [Field action] Let $U\subseteq x(	ext{laboratory region})=cI	imes\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a nonempty bounded open set whose closure is a compact subset of that chart image (chart coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0=ct$; [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), let $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, and let $A:N	o\mathbb R^4$, $x\mapsto(A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3)$, and $j:N	o\mathbb R^4$ be smooth ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); $A$ is a four-potential in the sense of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $j=(cho,J)$ is the four-current of [[def-em-sources]]. Write $A_
u:=\eta_{
u\mu}A^\mu$, $F_{\mu
u}:=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $F^{\mu
u}:=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{
u eta}F_{\alpha eta}$ and $j^
u A_
u$ for the indicated contraction, with the component dictionary $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ fixed in clause (a) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $\partial_\mu$ the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Define the **field action** by
$$S[A]:=c^{-1}\int_U\Bigl[- rac{1}{4\mu_0}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u\Bigr]d\lambda,$$
$d\lambda$ the four-dimensional Lebesgue measure in the chart coordinates ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]). Then $S[A]$ is a finite real number, in units of $\mathrm{J\,s}$: the density $-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u$ carries $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $d\lambda$ carries $\mathrm{m^4}$ and $c^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm{s\,m^{-1}}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). With $\kappa:=\mu_0$, $J:=j$ and the same bounded open $U$, one has $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{m math}[A]$, where $S_{m math}$ is the real functional of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]; since $c^{-1}>0$, the first variation and the stationarity of $S$ at $A$ are exactly those recorded there.

(b) [Admissible field variations] The field variations are the $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), extended by zero to $N$; for every real $s$ the field $A+sh$ is smooth on $N$, and $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ is the quadratic polynomial of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with both coefficients multiplied by $c^{-1}$. The field $A$ is **stationary** for $S$ if $ rac{d}{ds} ig|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(c) [Particle functional] Let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]] (a)), let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]	o A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a)), and let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$. The **particle functional** is the one of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]],
$$S_{m pt}[X]:=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds,$$
with admissible variations the fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations $h:[a,b]	o V$, $h(a)=h(b)=0$, of that lemma; $m$ is the external rest-mass parameter and $q$ the charge parameter of the framework, and $S_{m pt}$ is a finite real number on the declared class.

(d) [Scope] This item defines only the two functionals, their variation classes and the stationarity predicate; it asserts no stationarity of any configuration, no existence or uniqueness of stationary fields or curves, no boundary conditions, no convergence statement for unbounded regions, no coupled particle-field action and no dynamics of singular sources. Smooth $A$ and $j$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline U$ are required, and point or sheet sources are excluded ([[def-em-sources]] (b)). The physical adoption of stationarity is the postulate recorded later on this page (post-em-stationary-action-model).
items.strategy:
A definition assembled from earlier items, with well-definedness discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) Objects: the region, chart, indices and partial derivatives are those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; the component conventions $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$ and the potential and current dictionary are exactly clauses (a), (c), (d) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]; $j=(cho,J)$ and the charge parameter are those of [[def-em-sources]]. (ii) Finiteness: the density is smooth on the open neighbourhood $N$ and $\overline U$ is a compact subset of $N$, hence the density is bounded on $\overline U$; the bounded open $U$ has finite Lebesgue measure, so the integral is absolutely finite, and the stated physical units follow from the quantity table of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The functional is literally $c^{-1}$ times the mathematical functional $S$ of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] at $\kappa=\mu_0$ and $J=j$ on the same class of smooth fields and compactly supported variations; the lemma's statement (with its Countable Choice hypothesis) supplies the finiteness and the quadratic expansion used in (b), and multiplication by the positive constant $c^{-1}$ preserves first variations and stationarity. (iv) The particle integrals are finite-interval Riemann integrals, and that sector uses no Countable Choice. The particle functional is the exact functional of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]], cited rather than redefined; the identification of its curves with the framework's massive worldlines is clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]. (v) Scope: no choice beyond the inherited hypothesis, no existence, no boundary data, no singular sources, no coupled action.
items.physical_scope: Definition of two real functionals of the smooth finite-region model: the field action on a bounded chart region with a smooth prescribed four-current and compactly supported smooth field variations, and the fixed-endpoint particle functional on $C^2$ future timelike massive worldlines with a prescribed $C^2$ external four-potential. Excluded: existence or minimality of stationary configurations, boundary conditions, unbounded regions, singular sources, and any coupled particle-field action.

items.title: Adopt stationary Maxwell action as alternative physical formulation
items.statement:
The model adopts the following formulation principle as an alternative to postulating the field equations and the force law directly. (i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of clause (a) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is dynamically admissible exactly when it is stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$. (ii) [Particle sector] For a prescribed external four-potential $A_\mu$ on a neighbourhood of the image of a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline $X$, the motion is dynamically admissible exactly when $X$ is stationary for the particle functional $S_{\rm pt}$ of clause (c) of that definition under all fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations.

This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique, that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. No Noether theorem, no symmetry-to-conservation machinery and no matter dynamics beyond the prescribed potential are assumed. The conditional deductions of this pair are: on the declared smooth classes, (i) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor field equation $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and, for potential-represented fields, to the smooth-branch Maxwell equations, and (ii) is equivalent to the framework's adopted four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$; both deductions are recorded separately on this page, and this postulate asserts neither.
items.strategy: An explicit adopted-assumption contract, formulated by reference to the precise functionals, variation classes and stationarity predicate of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]. The non-derivation is deliberate: the postulate adopts a variational formulation of the same field and particle dynamics as an alternative model principle, and the conditional Euler-Lagrange calculations about the adopted functionals (the compact-variation field computation and the fixed-endpoint curve computation) are theorems recorded separately, not proofs of the postulate. The scope sentences exclude minimality, existence, uniqueness, symmetry-forcing, coupling and Noether content. The physical source context is the action-principle presentation of classical electrodynamics in the cited treatments, which likewise present stationarity as an adopted principle and do not prove it; the source row recording that the interaction form is not fixed by general considerations alone supports exactly this non-derivation scope. No choice principle is used by this item; its single formulation prerequisite carries the hypotheses noted there.
items.physical_scope: Adopted formulation principle: stationarity of the precisely defined smooth finite-region field action and of the fixed-endpoint particle functional under the declared variations, as an alternative presentation of the field equations and the force law. Not asserted: minimality, existence, uniqueness, symmetry-forcing, uniqueness of the action, coupling of the sectors, or any empirical claim.

items.title: Compact gauge variation is boundary-free for conserved source
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited through the componentwise fundamental-variation step of [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] and through [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. Let $U,N,A,j,F,S$ and the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]: $U$ bounded open with $\overline U$ compact in the laboratory chart image $cI	imes\Omega$, $N$ an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $A$ and $j$ smooth on $N$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $j=(cho,J)$ with the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], and $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U igl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u igr]d\lambda$. For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ write $\partial^\sharp\chi$ for the vector field with contravariant components $(\partial^\sharp\chi)^\mu:=\partial^\mu\chi=\eta^{\mu
u}\partial_
u\chi$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). It is a compactly supported smooth field variation. Thus $A^\mu\mapsto A^\mu+\partial^\mu\chi$ lowers to $A_
u\mapsto A_
u+\partial_
u\chi$; $A+\partial^\sharp\chi$ denotes this vector addition.

(a) [Exact gauge difference, no boundary term] For every such $\chi$ one has $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ on $U$, because $\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=0$ for the smooth $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); consequently the field term of $S$ is unchanged and
$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\,\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\,\chi\,d\lambda,$$
the second equality being the distributional integration-by-parts identity for the locally integrable fields $j^\mu$ and the smooth compactly supported $\chi$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); no boundary term arises precisely because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$.

(b) [Equivalence for smooth sources] If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$ (the source is conserved), then $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$. Conversely, if $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every such $\chi$, then $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise on $U$: the function $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on the open $U$ and pairs to zero against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$, so [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] applies. Hence for smooth prescribed sources the invariance of the field action under all compact gauge variations is equivalent to the conservation of the four-current.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair $(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(ho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause (a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ together with the cyclic identity). Then clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads $\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$; hence $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

(d) [Distributional reading] If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]), the gauge-difference pairing $c^{-1}\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle$ is defined for every test function $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ and equals $-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$ by the signed definition of the distributional derivative; hence the pairing vanishes for every compact gauge variation if and only if $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ as a distribution. This is a statement about the pairing only: the smooth $j$ of the definition is retained whenever the functional $S$ itself is used, and no products of distributions are formed.

Scope: the item computes the gauge variation of the field action and its compatibility with source conservation; it does not derive the field equations from gauge invariance, does not assert that conservation of a source implies stationarity, does not treat global or topological obstructions, and uses no Noether machinery.
items.strategy:
Direct finite computation plus the fundamental lemma. (a) Since $A^\mu$ is contravariant, the gauge variation is $\partial^\mu\chi$; lowering gives $\eta_{
u\mu}\eta^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\alpha\chi=\partial_
u\chi$. Since $A$ and $\chi$ are smooth, $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)+\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]; the quadratic field term is therefore constant along the gauge path, and only the source term changes: $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda$, using the linearity of the Lebesgue integral for the finite integrable functions ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Treat each $j^\mu$ as its regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]); the definition of the distributional derivative gives $\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle=-\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$, and for the $C^1$ field $j^\mu$ the distributional derivative equals the classical one ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]), which yields the displayed second equality. Because $\chi$ is compactly supported in the open $U$ there is no boundary term. (b) If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ identically, (a) gives invariance. Conversely $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on $U$, and the vanishing of its integral against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$ forces it to vanish pointwise by [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]]. (c) Under the smooth Maxwell branch, clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives the continuity equation; the chart identity $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J$ is the component computation of [[def-em-sources]] (c) and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], so (b) applies. (d) For a distributional $j^\mu$ the pairing identity is the definition of the distributional derivative, and the vanishing criterion is the definition of the zero distribution. The Countable Choice assumption enters exactly through the two cited conversions (the pointwise localization against all smooth tests and the classical-compatibility of the distributional derivative); no other choice principle is used.

Excluded: derivation of the field equations from gauge invariance, stationarity conclusions, global or topological obstructions, Noether machinery, and rough-source products.

items.title: Action stationarity implies the inhomogeneous Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]. Let $U\subseteq cI	imes\Omega$, $N$, the smooth fields $A,j$ on $N$, the components $A_
u$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $F^{\mu
u}$, the source convention $j=(cho,J)$, the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ and the field action $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U igl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u igr]d\lambda$ be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

Then the following are equivalent: (i) $A$ is stationary for $S$ under all $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, i.e. the adopted field equation of [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (i); (ii) $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ at every point of $U$ for every $
u\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

Consequently, if $A$ is stationary then: (a) [Inhomogeneous tensor equations] $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0 j^
u$ on $U$; (b) [Homogeneous tensor equations] $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}=0$ on $U$, since $A$ is smooth and its mixed partial derivatives commute; (c) [Laboratory Maxwell equations] define $\varphi:=-cA_0$, the spatial potential vector $\mathbf A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$, $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}\mathbf A$ by clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and $(ho,J)$ by $j=(cho,J)$ ([[def-em-sources]]); then on $U$ the four smooth-branch Maxwell equations hold, equivalently the eight scalar equations (TM1)-(TM2) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] hold with these fields and sources, i.e. $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

The statement concerns a given smooth pair $(A,j)$ on the declared region: it asserts no existence of a stationary field, imposes no boundary or decay condition, and excludes the weak, distributional, singular-support and non-potential-represented branches. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted stationary-action postulate and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy:
Instantiate the compact-variation lemma at $\kappa=\mu_0$ and $J=j$, then translate through the component equivalence. Since $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{m math}[A]$ with $c^{-1}>0$ and $S_{m math}$ the functional of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] on the same region and field class, the derivative of $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ vanishes for every $h$ exactly when that of $s\mapsto S_{m math}[A+sh]$ does; by clause (c) of that lemma this is equivalent to $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ for all $
u$ at every point of $U$. This proves (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii). Clause (b) is the closedness of the exact two-form: for smooth $A$ the cyclic sum $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}$ is a sum of six second partial derivatives of $A$ grouped in cancelling pairs by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]. Clause (c): the potential dictionary of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] identifies the components of $F$ defined here with those of the electromagnetic two-form built from $\varphi$ and $\mathbf A$; with clause (a) of that definition and $j=(cho,J)$, clauses (a) and (b) are exactly the systems (TM1) and (TM2), so clause (a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] - the component equivalence on the smooth branch, applied to these $C^\infty$ objects with the stated regularity - converts them into the four displayed equations and back. All derivatives are classical derivatives of smooth functions; the compact-support integration by parts is the supplied classical/weak-derivative compatibility calculation; no boundary term or rough-field weak-model claim is introduced, and the only choice assumption is the inherited one noted in the statement.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about a smooth four-potential and smooth prescribed four-current on a bounded chart region: stationarity of the adopted field action under all compactly supported smooth variations is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor equation, and stationarity implies the full smooth-branch Maxwell equations for the represented field pair and source. Excluded: existence of stationary fields, boundary and decay conditions, weak and distributional branches, singular sources, non-potential-represented fields, and any empirical claim.

items.title: Relativistic prescribed-field particle action yields the Lorentz force
items.statement:
The finite-interval Riemann particle-sector calculation is choice-free: the field-sector Countable Choice convention of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is not used here. Let worldlines, four-velocities and proper times be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form with the component and potential dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ be the framework's external rest-mass and charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)). Let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline (clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field - the prescribed external four-potential - on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$, and let $S_{\rm pt}$ be the particle functional of clause (c) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]], i.e. the functional $-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds$ of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]].

Then, under the adopted stationary-action model for the particle sector ([[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (ii)), for every fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation $h$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ is future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is stationary for $S_{\rm pt}$ under all such variations; (ii) $m\,dU_\nu/d\tau=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu$ on $[a,b]$, where $F=dA$ and $\tau$ is the proper time of $X$; (iii) the four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ of the framework's adopted covariant coupling [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], where $\Phi$ is the raised-index field operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$. In particular the stationary-action formulation of the particle sector is equivalent, for prescribed external potentials, to the adopted Lorentz coupling; the coordinate equations $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$ of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] then hold wherever the laboratory reading is $C^2$.

Scope: the potential, hence the field, is prescribed and external to the particle; the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence and any approximation of the trajectory over a time interval. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one massive charged particle on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed external $C^2$ four-potential: the fixed-endpoint stationarity of the particle functional is equivalent to the covariant four-force equation and to the adopted Lorentz coupling, with the coordinate force and power laws following. Excluded: self-field, radiation reaction, self-force, monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence, trajectory approximation, and any empirical claim.

items.title: Stationary functional need not be a minimum
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the field-action measure suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]); no additional choice is used. Work in [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the coordinate box $U=(-1,1)^4$ lying compactly inside the chosen laboratory chart, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) and $j=0$.

(a) [Coordinate and physical forms] With $x^0=ct$, set $U_t:=\{(t,x):(ct,x)\in U\}=(-1/c,1/c)\times(-1,1)^3$. The exact field dictionary gives
$$S[A]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U(|E|^2/c^2-|B|^2)d\lambda=\frac12\int_{U_t}(\varepsilon_0|E|^2-|B|^2/\mu_0)dt\,d^3x.$$
Also $S[\lambda A]=\lambda^2S[A]$ for every real $\lambda$.

(b) [Stationarity] $A=0$ is stationary: the actual first-variation coefficient of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] is $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$, and the action variation is $c^{-1}$ times its integral. Both terms vanish at $F=0,j=0$.

(c) [Positive direction] Choose $\theta\in C_c^\infty(U)$ with $\nabla_x\theta\not\equiv0$. Set the covariant components $h_0=\theta,h_i=0$, equivalently the contravariant variation $h^0=-\theta,h^i=0$. Then $E=c\nabla_x\theta$, $B=0$, and
$$S[h]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U|\nabla_x\theta|^2d\lambda>0.$$

(d) [Negative directions with a fixed compact support] Choose nonzero nonnegative smooth bumps $\eta,\varphi,\psi_2,\psi_3\in C_c^\infty((-1/2,1/2))$ using [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Extend them by zero to $\mathbb R$. For integers $N\ge1$ define the contravariant variation with only its second spatial component nonzero:
$$h^{(N)2}(x)=\eta(x^0)\varphi(Nx^1)\psi_2(x^2)\psi_3(x^3).$$
All supports lie in one fixed compact subset of $U$. Writing $f_N=h^{(N)2}$, its fields are $E=-c(\partial_0f_N)e_2$ and $B=-(\partial_3f_N)e_1+(\partial_1f_N)e_3$. Define finite constants, with all one-dimensional integrals over $(-1,1)$,
$$C_E=(\int\eta'^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2),\quad C_B=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi'^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2)>0,$$
$$C_3=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3'^2)\ge0.$$
Exact substitution and Fubini give
$$\int_U|E|^2/c^2d\lambda=C_E/N,\qquad\int_U|B|^2d\lambda=C_BN+C_3/N,$$
$$S[h^{(N)}]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\left(\frac{C_E-C_3}{N}-C_BN\right)\longrightarrow-\infty.$$
Thus a fixed sufficiently large $N$ supplies one negative direction $h_-$; the direction $h_+$ of (c) is positive. For nonzero $\lambda$, their rescalings keep their respective signs, and each action tends to zero in absolute value as $\lambda\to0$. A single fixed negative direction is not claimed to change sign under rescaling.

(e) [Every usual neighbourhood] Fix those two directions before rescaling. For each derivative multi-index, every compact-set supremum of a derivative of $\lambda h_\pm$ is $|\lambda|$ times the finite supremum for that fixed smooth compactly supported direction. Thus both tend to zero in the usual $C^k$, smooth compact-convergence and fixed-support and LF test-function topologies ([[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], [[def-test-function-topology]]) (and in any usual function-space topology with continuous scalar multiplication). Every such neighbourhood of zero therefore contains configurations of positive and negative action, arbitrarily small in magnitude. The stationary zero is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum. This is a computation in the declared smooth finite-region model, not a claim about actual fields or measurements; other sources or boundary/variation restrictions require their own analysis.
items.strategy:
(a) Substitute $\tfrac12F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ from [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] into the action. The coordinate change $x^0=ct$ has $d\lambda=c\,dt\,d^3x$ and changes the time interval to $(-1/c,1/c)$, so the physical-time formula uses $U_t$, not the unscaled coordinate box. Linearity of $F$ and the quadratic functional give the scaling law. (b) uses the exact raised-field/lowered-test coefficient and the overall factor $c^{-1}$ of the definition; at zero it vanishes pointwise.

(c) Direct differentiation gives the stated electric-only field. The continuous nonnegative integrand is positive on a small box because the spatial gradient is nonzero somewhere, so its integral is positive under the declared field-sector measure convention.

(d) Derive the three displayed field components by the product/chain rules. Every selected bump is smooth with compact support strictly inside $(-1/2,1/2)$, so all $h^{(N)}$ share an interior compact support. The nonzero compact bump $\varphi$ cannot have $\varphi'\equiv0$: FTC would make it constant on $\mathbb R$, and compact support would then force zero. Thus the continuous square $\varphi'^2$ is positive on an interval and has a positive integral; all undifferentiated bump-square integrals are likewise positive. For $N\ge1$, [[thm-substitution]] with the affine map $y=Nx^1$ gives $\int_{-1}^1\varphi(Nx^1)^2dx^1=N^{-1}\int_{-N}^N\varphi(y)^2dy=N^{-1}\int_{-1}^1\varphi(y)^2dy$, and the same identity for $\varphi'^2$. These are ordinary continuous compactly supported Riemann integrals; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] converts them to the action's Lebesgue integrals under the already-declared Countable Choice. [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] factors each smooth compact-support squared product. The time derivative supplies $C_E/N$; the $x^1$ derivative supplies $C_BN$, and the $x^3$ derivative supplies $C_3/N$. No endpoint touching the boundary and no false polynomial lower bound are used. Since $C_B>0$, choose one sufficiently large integer $N$ with negative action. Hold it fixed during rescaling.

(e) Quadratic homogeneity keeps the positive and negative signs separately. On the common fixed compact support, the seminorms $p_m$ of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]] obey $p_m(\lambda h)=|\lambda|p_m(h)$. In the LF definition [[def-test-function-topology]], every seminorm similarly obeys $q(\lambda h)=|\lambda|q(h)$, and a zero neighbourhood contains finitely many such bounds, so the line also tends to zero there. Scaling each fixed compact direction makes every derivative seminorm tend to zero and makes its action magnitude tend to zero. Hence every stated usual neighbourhood contains both signs, proving the full non-extremum claim without a claim that scaling a negative direction creates a positive one. This local functional counterexample is not a source's numbered physical result or an empirical assertion.
items.physical_scope: Worked computation in the smooth finite-region field action with the box region and no source: the stationary configuration of the adopted model is a saddle of the indefinite quadratic functional, with explicit compact variations of both signs and arbitrarily small magnitude. Excluded: any claim about physical fields or measurements, minimality of the adopted action, and applicability beyond the declared region and functional.

items.title: A compact test variation and gauge-source sign check
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited theorems. Work in the field-action setting of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with $U=(-1,1)^4$, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), and the component dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$.

(a) [Source-free zero field] For $j\equiv0$ and $A=0$ the first-variation coefficient (whose integral is multiplied by $c^{-1}$) $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] vanishes identically for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, because $F(A)=0$ and $j=0$; hence every compact first variation of $S$ at $A=0$ is zero and $A=0$ is stationary.

(b) [A non-trivial compact test variation] Let $A$ be the smooth potential with $A_0(x)=x^1$ and $A_1=A_2=A_3=0$, and let $j\equiv0$. Then $F_{01}=-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$ and all other components vanish, so the represented field is $E=(c,0,0)$, $B=0$ (clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) and $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=0$ on $U$. By the equivalence of [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]], $A$ is stationary; directly, for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ the first variation of $S$ at $A$ is
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=-\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_0h_1-\partial_1h_0\bigr)d\lambda=\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_1h_0-\partial_0h_1\bigr)d\lambda=0,$$
where each of $\int_U\partial_0h_1\,d\lambda$ and $\int_U\partial_1h_0\,d\lambda$ vanishes by the fundamental theorem in one variable combined with Fubini, and no boundary term appears because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

(c) [Gauge-source sign check with actual overlap] Independently choose the smooth prescribed source $j^0=c\rho(x^0)$, $j^i=0$, with nonzero nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty((-1/4,1/4))$ extended by zero. Choose $0\le\zeta\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ with $\zeta=1$ near $[-1/2,1/2]$, and nonzero nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1)^3)$, supplied by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Put $\varphi_\pm(u)=(2\pm u)\zeta(u)$ and $\chi_\pm(x)=\varphi_\pm(x^0)\psi(x^1,x^2,x^3)$. Both $\varphi_\pm$ are nonnegative compact bumps, but they are not globally monotone: on the entire support of $\rho$ their derivatives equal $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Use the contravariant gauge variations $(\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi_\pm$ from [[pthm-em-action-gauge-source-compatibility]]. Then
$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm]-S[A]=\left(\int_{-1}^1\rho\varphi_\pm'\,dx^0\right)\left(\int_{(-1,1)^3}\psi\,d^3x\right)=\pm\left(\int\rho\right)\left(\int\psi\right),$$
which is strictly positive for $+$ and strictly negative for $-$, since both factors are positive. Integration by parts gives exactly the same value as $-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi_\pm d\lambda$ with $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c\rho'$. This verifies the relative sign of the $+j^\mu A_\mu$ coupling, the raised-vector/covariant-lowered gauge shift and the conservation condition, using explicitly overlapping supports. If instead $\rho$ is constant on the whole neighbourhood, the source is conserved and every compact gauge difference is zero. No compact nonzero globally increasing or decreasing function is used.

(d) [Scope] The example is an exact computation in the declared smooth finite-region model; it asserts no existence of sources or fields, no numerical value of $\mu_0$, and no global gauge statement.
items.strategy: Direct substitution in the declared functionals. (a) is the first-variation formula of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with $F=0$ and $j=0$; the pointwise vanishing of the integrand gives a vanishing integral for every $h$. (b) The components follow from clause (a) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{01}=\partial_0A_1-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=\eta^{00}\eta^{11}F_{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$. The coefficient equation $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ holds because $F$ is constant and $j=0$, so [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] gives stationarity. The direct computation uses the first-variation expression of the cited lemma and the one-variable fundamental theorem for the compactly supported functions $h_0,h_1$, with Fubini reducing the four-dimensional integral; the absence of boundary terms is exactly the compact-support hypothesis. (c) Apply the corrected raised-gradient gauge formula. The cutoff $\zeta$ is one on a neighbourhood of the support of $\rho$, so $\zeta'=0$ there and $\varphi_+'=1$, $\varphi_-'=-1$ there. Although both compact functions must turn back to zero outside that plateau, those derivative changes do not meet $\rho$. Thus Fubini gives the two signed products of positive integrals exactly. The signs agree with one-dimensional [[thm-integration-by-parts]], whose endpoint term is zero because the factors are compactly supported. Constant $\rho$ instead gives $\int\rho\varphi_\pm'=0$ by FTC, consistently with source conservation. The prescribed source and potential here need not satisfy Maxwell together; this is the deliberately nonconserved-source functional witness, not a claim of a dynamically admissible source-field configuration. All relevant functions are smooth; the existing field-sector Countable Choice convention is retained.
items.physical_scope: Worked computation in the smooth finite-region field action on a box: the explicit first variation of a constant-field potential vanishes with no boundary term, and the exact gauge difference of the action pins the relative sign between the source coupling, the gauge shift and source conservation, including a non-conserved source exhibiting both signs. Excluded: existence statements, numerical values of constants, and any global or empirical claim.

items.title: Frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs and their real-field encoding
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary formulation prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set, and let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the vacuum constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Phasor encoding] For every pair of $C^\infty$ maps $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) define the **associated real fields** $$E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)\qquad((x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R),$$ componentwise, with the complex exponential and real part of [[def-complex-exponential]] and [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this is the encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] specialized from plane-wave amplitudes to a general $C^\infty$ amplitude, and the complex fields are not themselves physical fields. (b) [Source-free class] The pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ is called a **frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$** when it is $C^\infty$ and satisfies, on $D$, $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega\varepsilon_0\mu_0\widetilde E=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied componentwise to the complex fields. The word 'source-free' records that the displayed equations carry no charge or current term; the associated real fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]], $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $T:=2\pi/\omega$ the period. (c) [Status and scope] This item fixes the encoding, the four phasor equations and the terminology only. It asserts no equation for the associated real fields, no outgoing or boundary condition, no existence or uniqueness statement, no energy or flux reading and no empirical content. In particular the deduction that the associated real fields satisfy the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations with zero sources is not part of this definition; for the pairs used on this page it is established by the exterior-scattering theorem recorded later on this page. Only $C^\infty$ pairs on an open set are defined, so no boundary trace, weak or distributional class is introduced here.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract assembled from earlier items; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The encoding (a) is the real-part-of-complex-amplitude convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with a general $C^\infty$ spatial amplitude; the componentwise real part of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] are total on $\mathbb C^3$, so the associated real fields are defined for every $C^\infty$ pair, with no equation assumed. (ii) The class (b) is cut out by four equations on the open set $D$: the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] act componentwise on the $C^\infty$ complex fields, and the two constants satisfy $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=c^{-2}$ by [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the displayed third and fourth equations use only complex scalar multiplication, so the class is well-defined without any choice principle. (iii) The physical reading of the associated real fields as an electric and a magnetic field uses [[def-em-fields]]; the units of $\widetilde E$ are V$\,$m$^{-1}$ and those of $\widetilde B$ are T, inherited from that definition. (iv) Clause (c) records exactly what is not asserted; in particular the complex Maxwell-to-real-Maxwell deduction is deliberately left to a consumer, because a definition must not assert the field equations of its associated real fields.

items.title: Real parts of $e^{-i\omega t}$ phasors: calculus, injectivity and equivalence with the real Helmholtz-Maxwell system
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $c>0$ and $\omega>0$, and let $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$. Define $E,B:D\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the classes). Then: (a) [Calculus] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, then $E,B$ are $C^1$ and at every $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$: $\partial_tE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; for each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\partial_jE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\partial_j\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; and with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] acting on the spatial variable, $\operatorname{div}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{div}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, $\operatorname{curl}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$. (b) [Injectivity] if $w\in\mathbb C^3$ and $\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, then $w=0$; more generally, if $w:D\to\mathbb C^3$ is continuous and $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$, then $w\equiv0$ on $D$. (c) [Equivalence] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, the phasor system $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E$$ holds on $D$ if and only if the real system $$\operatorname{div}E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\quad\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ holds on $D\times\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: Write the encoding in real components: by the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=(\operatorname{Re}w(x))\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w(x))\sin(\omega t)$ componentwise, with the real and imaginary parts of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex arithmetic of [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. (a) For fixed $x$ each component is a constant-coefficient combination of $\cos(\omega t)$ and $\sin(\omega t)$; the affine map $t\mapsto\omega t$ has derivative $\omega$ by [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] applied to the differentiable real sine and cosine maps of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives their composite derivatives. The sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] then give $\partial_tE=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})$, and the spatial derivatives pass through the constant coefficients, giving the spatial formulas for each component; the divergence and curl formulas follow by applying the componentwise formulas and the linearity of [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]] (for complex fields, componentwise in real and imaginary parts). (b) Evaluating at $t=0$ gives $\operatorname{Re}w=0$; evaluating at $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ gives $\operatorname{Re}(-iw)=\operatorname{Im}w=0$ by the quarter-turn values of [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] and the Cartesian form of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so $w=0$. The continuous case applies the pointwise result at each $x\in D$; no choice principle is used. (c) Direction (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii): substitute the phasor equations into the calculus formulas of (a); e.g. $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)e^{-i\omega t})=\operatorname{Re}(i\omega\widetilde Be^{-i\omega t})=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})=c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Direction (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): subtract the complex expressions and apply (b), e.g. $\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E-i\omega\widetilde B)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)$ forces $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B$; the other three equations are analogous. All statements are pointwise algebraic identities; no PDE existence, no boundary condition and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$. (d) [Local solutions and exact global extension] Let I be any nonempty open interval, t* in I, and let z:I->R^n be C2 with the same harmonic equation on I. Then z=z_p+a+bt on I for a UNIQUE pair a,b, with b=z'(t*)-z_p'(t*) and a=z(t*)-z_p(t*)-bt*. The same explicit formula defines its unique global harmonic-ODE extension Z on R. This extension is T-periodic exactly when b0, equivalently z'(t*)=z_p'(t*); when b0 its mean over every complete period is a. For general drift, the mean of its global extension over [t,t+T] is a+b(t+T/2). Thus periodic preparation can be imposed on the global response without requiring a driven nonlinear family to exist on R. If I contains at least one pair t,t+T, equality at that pair forces b0. If I contains no such pair, a condition expressed only as z(t+T)=z(t) wherever both arguments belong to I is vacuous and does not imply periodicity of the global extension. All affine-drift local solutions remain classified, and the original global branches(a)-(c) remain intact.
items.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=a+bt$, and consequently $z=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used. For(d), apply the zero-derivative corollary on each closed subinterval of I to h'=z'-z_p', then to h-b id; any two points of the interval are contained in such a subinterval, so the constants agree throughout I. Evaluate at t* to get the displayed a,b, proving uniqueness. The explicit global formula is a solution on R by(a), and every other global solution extending z has the same value and derivative at t*, hence the same affine constants. Its period increment is bT, giving the periodicity equivalences and the single-pair test. Over every interval [t,t+T] the harmonic sine/cosine part has mean zero by scalar FTC. The affine part a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2), since its integral is aT+b[(t+T)²-t²]/2. Therefore the global extension z_p+a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2); it has mean a over EVERY complete period if and only if b=0. This last claim uses only ordinary finite-period integrals and no choice. The derivatives in(a) use the total chain rule [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] componentwise (or scalar coordinate-line chain rules), not a derivative rule asserted by the exponential definition alone.

items.title: The ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary model definition for the dipole scattering and Thomson items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $k:=\omega/c$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\mu_0>0$ the vacuum permeability of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $p_0\in\mathbb C^3$ (the complex dipole-moment amplitude, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m$). Define, on the punctured space $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ and all times $t\in\mathbb R$, $$E_{\rm d}(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(-\frac{\mu_0\omega^2}{4\pi r}\,n\times(n\times p_0)\,e^{i(kr-\omega t)}\Bigr),\qquad B_{\rm d}(x,t):=\frac1c\,n\times E_{\rm d}(x,t),$$ where $r:=|x|$ and $n:=x/r$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), with the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]] and the componentwise real-part encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] (the spatial amplitude here varies with x; no plane-wave instance is asserted). Call $(E_{\rm d},B_{\rm d})$ the **ideal harmonic electric-dipole radiation model of frequency $\omega$ and amplitude $p_0$**, and call $S_{\rm d}:=E_{\rm d}\times B_{\rm d}/\mu_0$ its model flux ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]); the model fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]]. [Adopted status] This is an explicitly adopted ideal radiation-law model, fixed by the following declarations: (i) it is the leading transverse far-zone field of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) evaluated at the harmonic transverse moment $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, i.e. at $p''$ for the waveform $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$; (ii) the model contains no independent magnetic-dipole or higher-multipole radiation, no near-zone or static field and no other radiating component; (iii) it is not asserted to solve the vacuum Maxwell equations at finite $r$, to be the field of any actual source, to satisfy any boundary condition or to have finite total energy on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$; (iv) for compact smooth conserved sources, comparison with these prescribed model fields uses the actual source's moment p_act(u), the harmonic waveform p_h(u)=Re(p0 exp(-i omega u)), their second-derivative mismatch M(u)=|p_act''(u)-p_h''(u)|, and the explicit D,Gamma bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]]. A bound depending only on that source's D and Gamma is valid when M0 on the observation window; the source's moment is not automatically the independently prescribed p0. These actual-source comparison uses assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) carried by the cited theorem. The explicit ideal fields themselves and their pointwise flux definition remain choice-free. No measured, empirical or material-response content is adopted: $p_0$ is prescribed model data, not a derived polarizability.
items.strategy: This is a definition contract; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The formula is the leading transverse term $E_{\rm lead}=\mu_0n\times(n\times V)/(4\pi r)$ of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]](c) at $V(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$: since $p''(u)=\operatorname{Re}(-\omega^2p_0e^{-i\omega u})$ for $p(u)=\operatorname{Re}(p_0e^{-i\omega u})$, the derivative supplied by [[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]](a) with w=-omega²p0, using its explicit C-infinity real harmonic waveform, the model field is exactly $E_{\rm lead}$ rewritten with $u=t-r/c$ and $e^{i(kr-\omega t)}=e^{-i\omega(t-r/c)}$; the cross product, inner product and norm are those of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. (ii) $r>0$ on the declared domain, so $E_{\rm d}$ and $B_{\rm d}$ are $C^\infty$ there and the same componentwise real-part convention as [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] is used; the varying radial amplitude is not a plane-wave amplitude; $E_{\rm d}\cdot n=0$ because $n\times(n\times p_0)$ is orthogonal to $n$, and $B_{\rm d}=n\times E_{\rm d}/c$ by definition. (iii) The model flux $S_{\rm d}$ is the quantity of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] evaluated at the model fields; that definition applies to any pair of fields of the declared regularity and assigns no field equation. (iv) The status clause lists the model assumptions (i)-(iv) and excludes exact Maxwell, source-realization, boundary, finite-energy and empirical claims; the model's relation to actual sources is only through the explicit bounds of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], which are quantified in the item below. The explicit formula/flux construction uses no choice. Actual compact-source comparisons retain the stated Countable Choice of [[pthm-em-dipole-radiation]], including a moment-mismatch term; no comparison to an arbitrary unrelated harmonic amplitude follows from D alone. Smoothness off r0 follows by coordinate sum/product/chain rules and the positive square-root/reciprocal powers of [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] for r=|x|; The harmonic lemma supplies all derivatives of the real waveform; compose its second derivative with u=t-r/c using the declared total chain rule. No complex-to-real derivative theorem is silently substituted for that real-waveform interface. Orthogonality is the finite cross-product identity of [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]] applied separately to real and imaginary components. The ideal model is meaningful also at p0=0, giving zero fields; no actual source realization or finite-radius Maxwell equation is deduced.

Excluded: exact Maxwell solutions at finite radius, near-zone and static fields, any actual source construction, boundary conditions, finite total energy, self-force and radiation reaction, material response laws, and every measured or empirical statement; the relation to actual compact smooth sources is only through the explicit error bounds of the dipole theorem.

items.title: Adopted scalar aperture-diffraction model (polarization-insensitive regime)
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the smooth modal full-Choice branch of the latter is not used. Adopt as a model assumption of the framework the following scalar aperture-diffraction model. [Data] Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ (the **aperture distribution**), with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. [Model field] The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude $$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$ where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted. [Adopted regime and status] The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.
items.strategy: This is an explicit adopted-assumption contract; it is deliberately not a derivation. (i) The mathematical object it adopts is the outgoing source field $u=G_k*\alpha$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], whose kernel and outgoing/Fraunhofer technique are fixed there. This model permits the compact closed-radius support $|y|\le a$, including aperture corners. Its integral and off-support regularity fall under that supplier by choosing any containing open ball of radius $A>a$; the sharp-radius estimates at $r\ge2a$ are proved directly in the consuming diffraction theorem, so this extension does not evaluate an open-support hypothesis at a boundary point; the integral against the finite complex measure is that of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. (ii) The physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the wavenumber-frequency relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The non-derivation clause is essential: neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity/material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model; the trace caveat is the one recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]. (iv) The scope sentences exclude exact Maxwell, vector, polarization, back-reaction, absolute-radiometric and empirical content. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers (the kernel lemma carries Countable Choice, as stated there). The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the cited kernel and boundary-representation suppliers; this postulate adds no choice use of its own.

Excluded: derivation from the vacuum Maxwell or material-closure postulates, exact Maxwell validity, identification of $\alpha$ with the exact screen boundary traces, well-posedness of simultaneously prescribed $u$ and $\partial_nu$, polarization and vector effects, aperture back-reaction, absolute radiometric calibration, apparatus, sampling and every empirical comparison.

items.title: Controlled scalar aperture diffraction: Fresnel and Fraunhofer approximations with explicit error terms
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] write $y_t=(y_1,y_2)$ and $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ for transverse vectors; for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $b\ge0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and any declared fixed small-angle range $(a+b)/z\le\eta_0<1$, where $0<\eta_0<1$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y_t|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.
items.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) The model field is the supplier's convolution. Choose any open containing ball of radius $A>a$ to obtain its off-support smoothness and Helmholtz equation. For the advertised sharp-radius endpoint, argue directly for every $|y|\le a$ and $r\ge2a$. Write $R=|rn-y|$, so $R\ge r-a\ge r/2$. For $h(s)=|rn-sy|$, the exact norm derivative formula from the supplier gives $|h''(s)|\le2a^2/(r-a)\le4a^2/r$; twice FTC therefore gives $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le2a^2/r$, and $|r/R-1|\le2a/r$. The supplier's real phase bound $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$ now gives $$\left|G_k(rn-y)-\frac{e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}}{4\pi r}\right|\le\frac1{2\pi r}\left(\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}r\right).$$ For a bounded continuous kernel $f$ on the compact support, $|\int f\,d\alpha|\le\sup|f|\,\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ follows by [[prop-simple-integrals-are-bounded-by-total-variation]] and uniform finite-simple approximation in [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; hence this pointwise bound proves the original field error, including $r=2a$. The exact derivative $\partial_rR=(r-n\cdot y)/R$ has modulus at most1 and $|\partial_rR-1|\le2a^2/r^2$. Differentiating the explicit kernel gives $r|\partial_rG_k-ikG_k|\le(\pi r)^{-1}(1+ka^2/r)$; the same finite-measure bound gives the uniform outgoing residual. All derivative passages under the source integral use the supplier's compact-product uniform difference-quotient argument, not an unsupported complex-measure dominated-convergence claim. (b) On the explicitly declared range put $d_0=a+b$ and $s=|\xi-y_t|^2/z^2\le\eta_0^2<1$. The actual supplier proof gives $|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le s^2/8$ and $|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le s/2$ by twice FTC. Consequently the phase error is at most $kd_0^4/(8z^3)$ and the relative amplitude error at most $d_0^2/(2z^2)$. The complex-measure kernel bound above gives $$|u-u_{\rm Fresnel}|\le\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{4\pi z}\left[\frac{d_0^2}{2z^2}+\frac{kd_0^4}{8z^3}\right],$$ which preserves and quantifies all original Fresnel estimates for the closed-support datum. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2\bigr|=\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|(|u_{\rm approx}|+|u|)$ together with $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$, obtained by applying the triangle inequality of [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]] in both directions; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.
